question: Should OpenClaw core accept this opt-in continuation subsystem, including trusted delegate-return delivery and configurable cross-session targeting, in PR #85651 after clean exact-head proof?
rationale: This is a new core agent lifecycle and security boundary, not a mechanical bug fix; the review can verify source and proof gaps but cannot choose the product/security posture for trusted cross-session context injection.

options.title: Require clean exact-head proof before merge
options.body: Keep #85651 open, require conflict resolution plus exact-head live proof for accepted `request_compaction`, Telegram delegate return, and trusted cross-session gating, then let maintainers decide final approval.

options.title: Split before core inclusion
options.body: Ask for smaller PRs that land the continuation substrate, security boundary, docs, and channel-visible behavior separately so each risk can be reviewed in isolation.

options.title: Accept the opt-in boundary now
options.body: Maintainers may decide the default-off config and existing corpus are enough, but they would own the cross-session trusted context-injection boundary and broad upgrade risk.

recommendation.title: Require clean exact-head proof before merge
recommendation.body: Keep #85651 open, require conflict resolution plus exact-head live proof for accepted `request_compaction`, Telegram delegate return, and trusted cross-session gating, then let maintainers decide final approval.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed this PR family, accepted parts of the core continuation shape, and explicitly identified cross-session targeting as a maintainer-deferred policy decision.
